biography:
Mika Wilson, a name whispered with both excitement and frustration in the New Zealand motorsport scene, hails from a small coastal town known more for its surfing than its speed. Growing up around her father's garage, Mika practically inhaled gasoline fumes before she could walk. Her racing journey began with go-karts, tearing up local tracks and quickly establishing herself as a force to be reckoned with. However, a tendency to either dominate or crash out of races quickly became her defining characteristic. 

Her big break came at 16 when she won the New Zealand Formula Ford Championship, a victory secured with a daring last-lap overtake that left seasoned veterans shaking their heads. This triumph propelled her into the world of open-wheel racing, but her inconsistent performance has been her Achilles heel. One race she's a podium contender, the next she's spinning out in the first corner. Despite this, her raw talent and undeniable passion keep her firmly on the radar of team managers and fans alike. 

Currently competing as an independent driver, scraping together sponsorship deals to keep her dream alive, Mika is at a critical juncture in her career. She possesses the speed and the ambition, but she needs to find the consistency to transform her potential into tangible results. The question isn't whether she has what it takes, but whether she can harness her wild energy into a controlled and focused performance.
drivingStyle: Mika's driving style is best described as 'all or nothing.' She attacks corners with a ferocity that borders on reckless, often pushing the limits of grip and flirting with disaster. Tire management is not her forte; she prefers to extract every last ounce of performance from the rubber in the early stages of a race, sometimes to the detriment of her later pace. Under pressure, Mika can either rise to the occasion with a stunning display of skill or crack completely, making costly mistakes. It's a high-risk, high-reward approach that keeps everyone on the edge of their seats.

rivalries.reason: Ricardo, a calculated and consistent driver, clashes with Mika's aggressive style. Their contrasting approaches often lead to on-track collisions and heated exchanges in the paddock.
Isabelle, known for her cool demeanor and strategic racing, represents everything Mika isn't. A rivalry rooted in contrasting personalities and perceived lack of respect from Mika.
Kenji and Mika frequently compete for the same sponsorships, leading to a tense off-track competition that spills onto the circuit.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks (unwashed) for every race.
Listens to heavy metal music at full volume right up until she gets into the car to 'get the adrenaline pumping'.
Refuses to walk under ladders, even when it's completely impractical to avoid them.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. You gotta go for it, even if it means crashing and burning."
careerHighlight: Winning the New Zealand Formula Ford Championship in 2020 with a spectacular last-lap pass that cemented her reputation as a fearless racer.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out on the first lap of the prestigious Auckland Grand Prix in 2022, eliminating herself and two other competitors in the process.
